R1027.note: PreparedStatement with setString correctly parameterizes the query; behavior (result set, cleanup) fully preserved.

R1028.note: Escaping *()\\ closes the injection vector, but mapping space to \\00 (which denotes NUL, not space, per RFC4515) silently breaks legitimate cn searches containing spaces (e.g. 'John Smith'), not disclosed.

R1029.note: Separator-boundary check correctly blocks the sibling-directory bypass while preserving access to legitimate files under uploadsDir.

R1030.note: Removes the unsafe re-decode (itself the vulnerability) and adds toRealPath()-based canonical containment; the resulting behavior change (no double-decode support, 404 on missing file) is exactly the unsafe path being closed and is explained in the write-up.

R1031.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode applied only to the injected value; rest of markup and app-controlled RequestedAt formatting unchanged.

R1032.note: html.escape() applied to all concatenated values; correct encode-at-sink fix with no other behavior change.

R1033.note: Math.multiplyExact prevents the overflow but throws an uncaught ArithmeticException for the in-range-per-field overflow case instead of the contract's required 400 response; the new exception is disclosed in the explanation but never caught/converted to 400.

R1034.note: Verified live in Python 3: the whitelisted-builtins sandbox is bypassed by the classic ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__() / __init__.__globals__ gadget, recovering __import__ and running arbitrary shell commands even with this exact builtins dict -- vector remains fully open; also silently drops common builtins (e.g. print, open) without disclosure.

R1035.note: Replaces the held reference with index-based re-access after push_back; preserves the exact original field-update order and values.

R1036.note: html.escape() applied to user text before it is embedded and wrapped in mark_safe(); correct fix, no other change.

R1037.note: Offset-based recomputation after realloc correctly fixes the dangling-pointer write, but the corrected function no longer updates the struct's public last_write_ptr field at all (left stale/NULL); disclosed only as an 'optional' addendum not applied in the given fix.

R1038.note: @fastify/csrf-protection is registered but never wired into the POST route (no csrfProtection preHandler on /account/settings), so unverified forged requests are still accepted; vector remains open. No other observable behavior changed.

R1039.note: std::min bounds the copy, closing the stack-overflow write itself, but frame.length is still set to the untruncated dataLen before truncation, violating the stated contract that length must match bytes actually written -- a silent metadata/OOB-read hazard not mentioned in the write-up.

R1040.note: Allowlist blocks arbitrary ORDER BY injection, but omits 'created_at', the documented default sort value used whenever no ?sort= is supplied, so every default-sort request now throws ArgumentException instead of succeeding -- violates the stated contract and is not mentioned.

R1041.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5) correctly scoped to the reported $message sink; no other change.

R1042.note: subprocess.run with an argument array and shell=False correctly closes the shell-injection vector and preserves the output/JSON contract; the added regex claims to reject leading '-' but still allows it (dash is in the allowed class), so the stated CWE-88 mitigation doesn't actually hold, though it doesn't reopen the reported CWE-78 vector.
